scope: East India Company and Indian paper-supply, packaging, sampling and quality-control infrastructure relevant as context for Hodgson's mixed paper stocks.
central_claim: Imported paper circulated through a multi-stage supply and quality-control system involving stationers, reams/quires, identifiable chests, presidency stocks, redistribution and physical musters. This infrastructure contextualizes Hodgson's imported/machine-made paper without proving the route of any specific Hodgson sheet.

nodes.source_family: Records of Fort St George: Despatches from England, 1724-27
operations: diagnosis that samples came from outside cording quires
supplier discrimination because Company used two stationers

quantity_structure.quire_sheet_count: 24 or 25 depending how the ream holds out

nodes.material_structure: outside cording/cassie quires contain torn, wrinkled, stained and otherwise inferior sheets, though usable sheets may be culled from them
nodes.control: technical comparator, not evidence for the exact constitution of a particular EIC ream beyond the Court's own description

primary_targets: IOR/E/4/887 p.112, Public Department letter, 11 June 1800
Fort St George Public Department, 4 September 1811

nodes.work: Robert Montgomery Martin, Eastern India, vol.1
market_structure: dedicated kaghazi paper shops in Patna
rough paper acquired wholesale from paper manufacturers
daftari office-oriented paper as a principal grade

operations: drawing paper treated as named stationery grade
proposal for half-yearly instead of annual drawing-paper supplies
nodes.control: seven years after Hodgson left Nepal; do not project as direct evidence of his supply route

quality_model: observed fitness = manufacture x grade/sorting x within-package position x finishing x stock history x transport x operation/interface x sampling procedure
source_control_rules: Do not infer that a Hodgson imported sheet came through Company stationery supply merely because the infrastructure existed.
Separate manufacture origin, supply node, issue node and use location.
Record ream/quire/package position when using physical samples as quality evidence.
Keep 1800-1811 IOR evidence at secondary-reconstruction status until primary items are directly read.
Keep Martin p.373 at page-specific secondary-control status until the page is directly inspected.
Treat 1850 drawing-paper administration as later continuity only.
next_actions: Directly inspect IOR/E/4/887 p.112 and related 1800-1811 targets
Identify the two London stationers in the 1725 Company supply if invoices survive
Search Hodgson/Residency accounts for ream, quire, chest marks, Stationery Office, stationer and drawing-paper issue language
Add package-position and supplier identifiers to the paper census
